competitive_landscape: Corsica Ferries and La Méridionale run the trunk car-ferry routes from the French mainland and Sardinia; intra-island water transport is dominated by seasonal day-tripper boats out of Bonifacio and Ajaccio with no high-frequency premium operator. Within Corsica, Air Corsica covers the Ajaccio↔Bastia trunk by air. None of this serves the Bonifacio Strait cross-border premium tier — Navier's opening lane.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the Corsica coastal spine and the Bonifacio Strait — Ajaccio→Bonifacio (~55 nm), Bonifacio→La Maddalena (~7 nm), Bastia→Cap Corse loops — all inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on protected lee water.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The hybrid Quanta-LR adds the Tyrrhenian extenders — Ajaccio↔Nice (~110 nm), Bastia↔Livorno (~80 nm), and the longer Corsica↔Riviera gateway runs — with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

precedents.why_it_matters: Bonifacio↔La Maddalena (~7 nm) wires Corsica directly into the existing Costa Smeralda atlas node — a clean intra-Schengen extension rather than a cold net-new build.

regulatory_note: Mediterranean SOx-ECA applies from 2025 with FuelEU Maritime layered on top. Scandola is a UNESCO World Heritage marine reserve with active wake/anchoring restrictions, and the Gulf-of-Porto overlay gives a textbook quiet-mode/zero-emission entry argument. The Bonifacio Strait is a recognised IMO Particularly Sensitive Sea Area (PSSA) — additional emissions/anchoring discipline applies. France's national MPA framework is among the most aggressive enforcers in the Western Med.
seasonality: Peak July–August (the ~8M visitor surge), shoulder May–June and September–October on Mediterranean weather, and a low-volume winter where the coastal spine becomes a thinner local-services run. Western coast (Calvi, Scandola) is more exposed than the eastern lee; the Bonifacio Strait sees mistral/sirocco bursts that the foiling platform handles materially better than displacement RIBs.

summary: Corsica concentrates ~8M visitor-arrivals into a short summer, with Ajaccio (~2.38M passengers) and Bastia (~3.28M) ports anchoring a coastal spine and pocket archipelagos — Lavezzi, Cavallo, and the Scandola/Gulf-of-Porto UNESCO reserve. The defining asset is the Bonifacio Strait: Bonifacio↔La Maddalena/Costa Smeralda is ~7 nm of low-friction intra-Schengen water that ties Corsica directly to the already-built Sardinia node. A Pioneer II spine (Ajaccio→Bonifacio→Bastia) plus a Quanta-LR Tyrrhenian extender to Côte d'Azur and Liguria.
